newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia expects fresh World Bank loans.
newsitem.headline: Croatia expects fresh World Bank loans.

text.p: The World Bank will soon approve new loans to help Croatia overhaul its banking system and restructure its pension plan, Croatian state media said on Thursday.

"We confirmed support the Bank is able to offer Croatia," World Bank head James Wolfenshon told Croatian television (HRT) after meeting Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa, who is on a visit to the United States.

Matesa told HRT the bank was likely to approve a $100 million EFSAL loan aimed at overhauling troubled Privredna, Splitska and Rijecka banks, as well as ailing state firms such as oil concern INA, Croatian railways, telecom HPT and others.
The $100 million loan should be approved in May, the state news agency HINA said.
"As far as EFSAL is concerned, that's settled," Matesa told HRT.
HINA said the World Bank was preparing another $80 million loan to restructure Croatia's pension system.
The bank has so far approved nine projects totalling $450 million for Croatia's reforming economy.
